1.why: Every MFA endpoint goes through authorized(), which requires a session userId that maps to an account and never accepts a client-supplied account id.

2.why: Identity OTPs are bound to the session challenge hash, TOTP to the account secret, and recovery codes to that account’s backup map, so a code cannot be reused for a different user.

3.why: Enabling MFA (authenticator verify / backup confirm) never deletes or invalidates other sessions that share the same userId; only the current session is advanced.

4.why: The authenticator seed is stored with AES-256-GCM encrypt(), and recovery codes are stored only as peppered SHA-256 hashes in account.backups.

5.why: Secrets and codes are produced with crypto.randomBytes / randomInt (CSPRNG); fixed demo values are only used when DEMO_MODE is on.

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly; there is no localStorage/sessionStorage of secrets/OTPs/tokens—only in-memory JS during setup and HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validates email (emailOK), OTP (otpOK), recovery format (codeOK), method allow-list, body shape/size, and password length before use.

8.why: Client renders dynamic values with textContent/JSON and the HTML shell is static with a nonce CSP, so injected markup is not executed.

9.why: No redirect endpoints or user-controlled redirect parameters exist; navigation stays on same-origin API/UI paths only.

10.why: securityHeaders() sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors 'none', and related hardening headers on responses.

11.why: cookieValue() sets mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict.

12.why: Generic 500 messages hide stack traces; secrets are not written to server logs or URLs (demo codes only go to the browser console by design).

13.why: Identity/fixture codes have expires and used flags; recovery codes are marked used; TOTP is time-windowed with PERIOD.

14.why: failed()/isLocked() apply a 5-attempt, 15-minute lockout on sign-in, identity, authenticator, and recovery, plus identity request throttling.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the old session and issues a new id; idle/absolute timeouts are enforced in getSession; logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
